title: Tiered regional failover harness with adaptive load-shedding and silent-dep simulation
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build and run a deterministic test harness that simulates ordered regional degradations combined with staggered GPU pool exhaustion and 'silent' dependency failures (requests accepted by a dependency but never responded to). The goal is to validate: 1) multi-region failover correctness for tenant-priority routing, 2) circuit-breaker and backpressure policies on the edge and runtime, 3) adaptive load-shedding decisions and their alignment with SLOs (p99 latency, success rate), and 4) safety of automated rollback and eviction policies under tenant mix. This harness must be repeatable, parameterizable (duration, intensity, affected regions/pools), and produce time-aligned traces and cost/accounting delta reports.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible scenarios for (a) single-region silent-dep, (b) GPU-pool drain in primary region with regional failover, and (c) simultaneous silent-dep + pool-exhaustion
No customer-facing SLO breaches for high-priority tenants in canary runs (tracked via canary token list) beyond the agreed threshold
Circuit breakers trip and recover as configured with evidence in traces and logs
Adaptive load-shedding decisions recorded and match policy thresholds (eg shed low-priority at 65% pool pressure)
Playbook documented and a one-click abort/rollback implemented for the experiment
runbook_steps: Provision test tenants: 3 priority tiers (high, medium, low) with synthetic request profiles
Create traffic generator with realistic seq-length and KV-cache hit-rate distribution
Start baseline run for 30 minutes to capture normal metrics
Inject silent-dep in region-us-east-1 for 5m, measure request queue growth and circuit-breaker events
After 2m of silent-dep, start progressive GPU pool drain on same region (20% -> 60% -> 95%) with 60s hold per step
Observe routing: requests should failover to us-west-2 or eu-central-1 based on latency SLO and tenant policy
Enable adaptive load-shedding policy at 50% pool pressure increment and validate token-level decisions
Run post-mortem capture, collect flamegraphs, kv-cache metrics, token-level cost deltas, and trace spans
safety_controls: Canary scope limited to explicit test tenant tokens (no production tokens)
Kill-switch API that immediately restores normal routing and drains injected faults
Automated abort if p99 latency for high-priority tenants exceeds 2000ms for >2 minutes
Rate-limited injection ramp (max 20% of baseline RPS change per minute)
Observation-only dry-run mode available to validate instrumentation before full injection
metrics_to_record: p50/p90/p99 latency per tenant-priority and per region
success_rate (2xx) and error_budget burn by tenant and route
trace span durations for dependency calls and runtime scheduling delays
cost_delta_per_token and inferred token CPU/GPU cycles
experiment_results: Initial canary (low intensity) completed 2025-02-25. Observations: silent-dep produced rapid queue growth in the runtime dependency proxy within 30s; circuit breakers opened for medium and low tenants but delayed for high tenants due to priority exemptions. Adaptive shedding triggered correctly at 62% measured pool pressure but was too conservative: low-priority shed rate peaked at 48% while queue growth continued in the dependency proxy. Failover routing to secondary region increased p99 by 22% but maintained success rate for high tenants. No data plane panic observed. Follow-up required to tighten shedding thresholds and to add early dependency timeouts in the proxy layer.
next_steps: Tweak adaptive shedding thresholds: lower low-priority threshold from 65% to 55% and add hysteresis
Introduce soft-dependency-timeout in proxy at 800ms with exponential backoff
Re-run medium-intensity experiment with tenant mix skew (50% low, 30% medium, 20% high)
Wire up automated post-run report generation for stakeholders (PM/SE/Oncall)
Schedule cross-team review with Console/Runtime/Proxy owners (owners list in artifacts)
